suggestions.title: Lion's mane and ashwagandha: your warning, five tries, all AI

inserts.text: Lion's Mane & Ashwagandha: I'm not advising either of these. They're popular for focus and stress, but unfortunately some people report anhedonia (when nothing feels good anymore) and sexual dysfunction that hangs around even after they stop taking them--people call it post-ashwa or post-lion's mane syndrome. It's rare, but it's the same kind of thing SSRIs and finasteride can do, so it's something to keep in mind.

suggestions.title: Agmatine's stop signs with your lasting-anhedonia warning: three tries, all AI

edits.before: Stop immediately if it causes flatness, anhedonia, apathy, emotional blunting, new depression, agitation, irritability, insomnia, dizziness, palpitations, nausea, loose stools, diarrhea, or increased craving. Only the stomach problems showed up in the human trials, but the flatness happens in practice, so do not "push through" numbness. If agmatine makes the world more gray, it is the wrong tool for that phase.
edits.after: Agmatine can leave you flat and numb--people do get that in practice, even if the human trials only turned up stomach problems--so stop it right away if you notice you're flatter or more depressed than before you started, things stop feeling good, or you just stop caring. Same if it winds you up instead (more irritable, can't sleep), or you get dizziness, palpitations, nausea, loose stools or stronger cravings. Unfortunately a few people say the numbness hung on for weeks after they quit, so don't push through it hoping it'll settle like side effects sometimes do.
